options: Self-attention uses softmax, cross-attention doesn't
In self-attention, Q, K, and V all come from the same sequence; in cross-attention, Q comes from a different sequence than K and V
Cross-attention never uses a scaling factor
Self-attention can only be used in encoders, cross-attention only in decoders
questions.explain: Self-attention projects Q, K, V from one shared sequence; cross-attention sources the query from a different sequence than the key and value.

questions.q: In an encoder-decoder transformer used for translation, what does cross-attention let the decoder do?
options: Attend over its own previously generated tokens only
Attend over the full encoder output while generating each target token
Skip the attention mechanism entirely
Directly copy the encoder's weights
questions.explain: Cross-attention lets the decoder's query look back at the encoder's key/value representations of the full source sentence at every generation step.

questions.q: If a decoder's query sequence has length 6 and the encoder's key/value sequence has length 10, what shape does the cross-attention output have?
options: Length 10, matching the key/value
Length 16, the sum of both lengths
Length 6, matching the query
This configuration is not allowed in PyTorch
questions.explain: Attention produces one output per query position, so the output's sequence length always matches the query's length, regardless of the key/value length.

questions.q: Why is it mathematically valid for Q and K to come from sequences of different lengths in cross-attention?
options: Because PyTorch automatically pads the shorter sequence
Because scaled dot-product attention only requires Q and K to share their last (feature) dimension, not their sequence-length dimension
Because cross-attention doesn't actually compute a dot product
It isn't valid — Q and K must always have the same sequence length
questions.explain: The Q @ Kᵗ dot product only requires matching feature dimensions; the sequence-length dimensions of Q and K are independent of each other.

questions.q: In code, calling mha(x, x, x) versus mha(decoder_hidden, encoder_output, encoder_output) — what's the key difference?
options: The first uses a different attention formula than the second
The first passes the same tensor as query/key/value (self-attention); the second passes a different tensor as query than as key/value (cross-attention)
There is no difference; both always produce identical results
The second call is invalid syntax in nn.MultiheadAttention
questions.explain: mha(x, x, x) is self-attention because all three arguments are the same sequence; mha(decoder_hidden, encoder_output, encoder_output) is cross-attention because the query differs from the key/value source.
